name: Conditions
description: General rules governing conditions. Individual condition effects are defined once in data/native/conditions.json.
entries: A condition alters a creature's capabilities and can arise from spells, class features, attacks, the environment, or other effects. Some conditions are beneficial.
A condition lasts until it is countered or for the duration specified by the effect imposing it.

If multiple effects impose the same condition, each instance retains its own duration, but the condition's effects do not increase merely because it is applied more than once. Exhaustion is an explicit exception: it accumulates in levels as defined by its own rule.

Conditions can apply other conditions. Their effects are cumulative, subject to the normal rules for simultaneous effects. When an inherited condition ends, other independently applied instances of that condition remain in force.
Refer to the canonical condition records for the actual effects, restrictions, and ending triggers. Source-edition definitions are retained separately as historical evidence.

For attacks using Armor Class, calculate the applicable normal or Touch defense from the target's contributions, then apply only the applicable defensive effects from its conditions. Denial of Dexterity defense is not itself the full Flat-Footed condition. See data/native/defenses.json.

Historical 3.x conditions are normalized into independent native records. Dazed does not imply loss of Concentration, while Nauseated explicitly ends Concentration. Compound skill checks and repeated impairment of the same underlying statistic must not apply the same modifier more than once.

Fear-based conditions can impose different severities and sources. Do not treat Shaken, Frightened, Panicked, and Cowering as synonyms. The 3.x automatic escalation of multiple fear effects remains a separate, unresolved native policy; direct Panicked-to-Cowering behavior when escape is impossible is defined on Panicked.

Fatigued and six-level Exhaustion remain distinct. Applying an additional fatigue effect does not silently map the historical 3.x Exhausted condition onto an unapproved native Exhaustion level; the source-to-native compatibility mapping must be reconciled explicitly.

Held and Pinned have different origins and defenses. Held includes Helpless and retains awareness unless another effect states otherwise; Pinned includes Grappled without Helpless. Escape from Pinned leaves Grappled active when its own source remains in effect.
